$comment: Paladin settings key list — source of truth for the settings form, validation, tooltips, and gotcha surfacing (scope doc §6.2). Community PRs welcome: this file is data, not code.

template_verified.result: 119/119 template keys covered, all template defaults match; +1 deprecated key retained for EA-config parsing; 1 in-game flag remains (bInvisibleOtherGuildBaseCampAreaFX polarity)

verification_status: VERIFIED against a live 1.0.1 DefaultPalWorldSettings.ini (2026-07-27, testbox). Remaining non-empty 'verify' arrays mark questions a template diff cannot answer (in-game behavior) and must be checked before the relevant UI ships. 'source' records provenance: official = Pocketpair 1.0 docs; community = current community docs verified against live 1.0 servers; ea-carryover = present since Early Access, carried into 1.0; deprecated = officially superseded.

file_format.structure: Exactly two lines: '[/Script/Pal.PalGameWorldSettings]' then one OptionSettings=(k=v,k=v,...) line.
serialization_rules: No spaces, no line breaks inside OptionSettings.

global_gotchas.text: A malformed OptionSettings line (stray newline, unbalanced quote/bracket, lowercase 'true') does NOT error — the server boots normally with 100% default settings and silently ignores the whole file. Paladin's post-APPLY structural validation exists for exactly this.
The ini is read once at boot; no reload, no hot-apply. The basis of the commit-and-restart workflow.

Once a world exists, a WorldOption.sav in the save folder is read IN PREFERENCE to PalWorldSettings.ini for the values it contains — later ini edits silently do nothing for those keys on that world. Community consensus; which exact keys it covers on a 1.0 dedicated server must be test-box verified. The settings module must detect WorldOption.sav and warn per-affected-key at commit time.
global_gotchas.confidence: community-consensus; verify scope on test box

global_gotchas.text: Community claim that the server rewrites the ini from memory on shutdown: TESTED AND NOT REPRODUCED on v1.0.1.100619 (2026-07-27) — a marker edit made while running survived a graceful stop with an unchanged file hash. Paladin's APPLY-after-STOP ordering is retained anyway: it is correct under both realities and future patches could change this.
Command-line arguments to PalServer beat the ini. Paladin owns the systemd unit, so it must keep the ExecStart line free of settings args (or treat any it sets as ini-read-only).

GET /v1/api/settings (the VERIFY readback source) has two verified quirks on v1.0.1.100619: (1) AdminPassword and ServerPassword are never returned (keys carry rest_readback:false; VERIFY reports them as applied-but-not-readback-verifiable, file authoritative); (2) at least one key returns with DIFFERENT CASING than the ini (AutoSaveSpan -> autoSaveSpan), so readback matching must be case-insensitive across the board.
DefaultPalWorldSettings.ini at the install root is a never-read template. The live file is Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer/PalWorldSettings.ini.

keys.tooltip: Server name shown in the in-game community server browser.
Description shown under the server name in the browser.
Password required to join the server. Empty = open join.
Password for in-game admin commands, RCON, and the REST API.
keys.gotcha: One shared credential covers every privileged interface, and REST/RCON transmit it over unencrypted HTTP Basic auth. Make it long and never expose these ports beyond localhost/LAN.
keys.protected: Paladin authenticates to the server with this password — changing it here would break Paladin's access. Change manually and update Paladin's environment together.

keys.tooltip: Maximum concurrent players.
keys.gotcha: 32 is a hard engine ceiling. Higher values silently clamp to 32.

keys.tooltip: Co-op party size cap.
keys.gotcha: Widely reported as non-functional on dedicated servers — the co-op limit stays at 4 regardless of this value.

keys.tooltip: Require platform authentication for connecting players.
keys.gotcha: Disabling removes identity verification — a large security hole for no real gain.

keys.tooltip: URL the server pulls a global ban-list feed from.
keys.gotcha: This is Pocketpair's global feed, not the server's own bans — those live in Pal/Saved/SaveGames/banlist.txt. Don't point this at arbitrary URLs.

keys.tooltip: Region label for the server listing.
Multiplayer flag for co-op session settings.
keys.gotcha: Template-verified present with default False; believed irrelevant on dedicated servers.

keys.tooltip: Superseded platform-restriction key.
keys.gotcha: Officially "Not available in this version. Use CrossplayPlatforms instead." VERIFIED absent from the 1.0.1 template — kept so the parser recognizes it in adopted EA-era configs; render read-only/hidden.

keys.tooltip: Which platforms may connect to the server.
keys.gotcha: Console and Game Pass players can ONLY join via the in-game community-server browser (no direct-IP field exists for them). Restricting platforms, or an unfindable server name, silently locks them out even though the server runs fine.

keys.tooltip: Allow players with client mods enabled to join.
Display the creator's player ID on structures.
keys.gotcha: A moderation tool on public servers: see who built the thing blocking the path.

keys.tooltip: Show in-game chat messages when players join or leave.
Enable the game's own rolling save backups (backup/ dir in save data).
keys.gotcha: Increases disk load. Cadence: 5 saves @30s, 6 @10min, 12 @1h, 7 @1day. Independent of Paladin's backup system — budget disk for both.

keys.tooltip: Maximum chat messages per player per minute.
Server log output format.
(Community server) Explicit external public IP to advertise.
(Community server) External public port to advertise.
keys.gotcha: Advertisement only — does NOT change the port the server listens on; the listen port is a command-line argument.

keys.tooltip: Enable the RCON remote console.
keys.gotcha: RCON is deprecated in favor of the REST API; Paladin uses it only as a fallback.

keys.tooltip: TCP port for RCON.
Enable the official REST API.
keys.gotcha: Paladin requires this ON. Pocketpair explicitly warns the API must not be exposed directly to the internet — keep it on localhost/LAN.
keys.protected: Paladin controls the server through the REST API — disabling it would sever Paladin's connection. Change manually only if you know what you're doing.

keys.tooltip: TCP port for the REST API.
keys.protected: Paladin connects to the REST API on this port — changing it would sever Paladin's connection. Change manually only if you know what you're doing.

keys.tooltip: Total number of base camps allowed across the whole server.
keys.gotcha: A server-wide budget: on a full 32-player server, 128 is only 4 bases per player.

keys.tooltip: Maximum base camps per guild.
keys.gotcha: LEVEL-GATED: raising this raises the cap, but guilds still unlock base slots progressively through in-game progression — the extra slots will NOT appear immediately after restart. The setting has applied even though nothing visibly changed. Also raises processing load (official note).

keys.tooltip: Maximum Pals working at one base.
keys.gotcha: Widely and persistently reported as non-functional on dedicated servers — stuck at 15 regardless of value. Set it, restart, and check in-game; if it didn't move, that's the game, not the config. Also raises processing load (official note).

keys.tooltip: How often an open container UI force re-syncs (seconds).
keys.gotcha: Raising it makes chest contents feel laggy for a marginal saving.

keys.tooltip: Per-player structure cap. 0 = unlimited.
keys.gotcha: On public servers, one player with unlimited structures is a performance problem for everyone.

keys.tooltip: Cap on dropped items simulating full physics. -1 = unlimited.
keys.gotcha: Best new performance key in 1.0. Default -1 (unlimited) lets a littered base become a physics workload; 200-500 is a sane cap.

keys.tooltip: Distance (cm) from players within which Pals are replicated to clients.
keys.gotcha: Official min/max 5000-15000. Lower = less bandwidth/CPU, but distant Pals pop in later.

keys.tooltip: Guilds processed per server frame.
How often Pal storage is re-checked (seconds).
Cache lifetime for the builder-name lookup on structures (seconds).
Enable fast travel.
Restrict fast travel to between the player's own bases only.
Let players choose their starting location on the map.
keys.gotcha: Default VERIFIED False against the 1.0.1 template (2026-07-27) — earlier published sources disagreed.

keys.tooltip: Players' bodies remain in the world (sleeping) after logout.
Enable base raid invasions.
keys.gotcha: Disabling raids is a well-known memory-load mitigation, but 1.0 rebuilt raids into a wave system that scales with your base — turning them off deletes headline 1.0 content. Prefer scheduled restarts (Paladin's RAM-threshold restart) instead.

keys.tooltip: Hardcore mode: no respawn on death.
Allow recreating a character after hardcore death.
keys.gotcha: If bHardcore is on and this is off, one death permanently ends that player's participation.

keys.tooltip: Party Pals are permanently lost on player death.
keys.gotcha: Deletes hours of breeding work in one accident. Distinct from DeathPenalty.

keys.tooltip: Pal spawn randomization mode.
Seed for the spawn randomizer (reproducible randomized worlds).
If true, wild Pal levels are fully random rather than area-appropriate.
Allow saving Pals to the account-wide Global Palbox.
Allow importing Pals from the account-wide Global Palbox.
keys.gotcha: The most consequential toggle for a public server: left on, anyone can arrive day one with a fully-bred endgame roster.

keys.tooltip: Automatically delete structures and base Pals of fully-inactive guilds.
keys.gotcha: This deletes players' bases. Pair with a generous threshold below.

keys.tooltip: Hours of total guild inactivity before auto-reset triggers.
keys.gotcha: Ignored unless bAutoResetGuildNoOnlinePlayers is True (official note). 72h is not a long holiday — consider 168+.

keys.tooltip: Prevent building near structures such as fast-travel points.
Hide other guilds' base-area boundary effects.
keys.gotcha: Naming is inverted vs the official description ("Show base area boundaries") — verify polarity in-game before documenting UI labels.

keys.tooltip: Show the online player list on the ESC menu.
In-game proximity voice chat (dedicated servers only).
keys.gotcha: Dedicated-server exclusive and off by default. Does NOT work for Microsoft Store / Game Pass PC clients — those players still need external voice.

keys.tooltip: Distance within which voices are heard at full volume (game units; ~100 = 1m).
Distance at which voices fade to silence (game units).
Allow allocating Statue of Power points to HP.
Allow allocating Statue of Power points to Stamina.
Allow allocating Statue of Power points to Attack.
Allow allocating Statue of Power points to Carry Weight.
Allow allocating Statue of Power points to Work Speed.
Aim assist for controller players.
Aim assist for mouse-and-keyboard players.
Enable the penalty system for extended non-login.
Roaming Predator boss Pals in the world.
keys.gotcha: Note: no 'b' prefix — the key really is EnablePredatorBossPal.

keys.tooltip: Master PvP flag for the world.
keys.gotcha: Does almost nothing alone. Working PvP needs THREE keys: bIsPvP, bEnablePlayerToPlayerDamage, and bEnableDefenseOtherGuildPlayer. Missing any one produces a broken-feeling half-PvP server.

keys.tooltip: Players can damage each other.
keys.gotcha: Part of the required PvP trio — see bIsPvP.

keys.tooltip: Base defense Pals attack players from other guilds.
keys.gotcha: Part of the required PvP trio — see bIsPvP.

keys.tooltip: Players can damage members of their own guild.
Players may loot other guilds' death-penalty drops.
Drop a special extra item when a player is killed in PvP.
Item ID of the extra PvP-kill drop.
Quantity of the extra PvP-kill drop.
Show player locations and PvP-item counts on the world map.
Show each base's PvP-item count on the world map.
Named difficulty preset.
keys.gotcha: Reported to have little or no effect on its own — the individual multipliers are what actually change the game.

keys.tooltip: Daytime progression speed multiplier.
Nighttime progression speed multiplier.
Experience gain multiplier.
Pal capture rate multiplier.
Wild Pal spawn density multiplier.
keys.gotcha: Official note: impacts performance — every extra spawn is a ticked AI actor.

keys.tooltip: Damage dealt by Pals multiplier.
Damage taken by Pals multiplier.
Damage dealt by players multiplier.
Damage taken by players multiplier.
Player hunger depletion multiplier.
keys.gotcha: Key is genuinely misspelled ("Decreace") in the game. "Fixing" the spelling silently disables the setting — the game ignores unknown keys without warning.

keys.tooltip: Player stamina depletion multiplier.
keys.gotcha: Key is genuinely misspelled ("Decreace") in the game. "Fixing" the spelling silently disables the setting — the game ignores unknown keys without warning.

keys.tooltip: Player natural HP regeneration multiplier.
keys.gotcha: Casing quirk: 'HP' here but 'Hp' in the InSleep variant. Copy exactly.

keys.tooltip: Player HP regeneration while sleeping multiplier.
Pal hunger depletion multiplier.
keys.gotcha: Key is genuinely misspelled ("Decreace") in the game. "Fixing" the spelling silently disables the setting — the game ignores unknown keys without warning.

keys.tooltip: Pal stamina depletion multiplier.
keys.gotcha: Key is genuinely misspelled ("Decreace") in the game. "Fixing" the spelling silently disables the setting — the game ignores unknown keys without warning.

keys.tooltip: Pal natural HP regeneration multiplier.
keys.gotcha: Casing quirk: 'HP' here but 'Hp' in the InSleep variant. Copy exactly.

keys.tooltip: Pal HP regeneration while in the Palbox multiplier.
Base-Pal work speed multiplier (crafting, building, hauling).
keys.gotcha: Not in the official 1.0 parameter table but present in the file and the single most-tuned setting in the game.

keys.tooltip: Structure health multiplier.
Damage taken by structures multiplier.
Structure decay speed multiplier. 0 disables decay.
keys.gotcha: 0 is a deliberate, supported choice for burst-play communities — bases don't crumble during a week away.

keys.tooltip: Yield multiplier for gatherable nodes (ore, trees, etc).
Health multiplier for gatherable objects.
Gatherable-object respawn INTERVAL multiplier.
keys.gotcha: INVERTED: this is an interval, not a speed. LOWER = FASTER respawns. Setting 2.0 expecting faster respawns makes them twice as slow. Use 0.5 to double respawn speed.

keys.tooltip: Dropped-loot quantity multiplier from enemies.
What players drop on death.
keys.gotcha: Default VERIFIED as Item against the 1.0.1 template (changed from EA's All) — adopted EA configs may still carry All, which is harsher than most groups expect. Enum meanings — None: no drops; Item: all items except equipment; ItemAndEquipment: all items; All: all items AND all party Pals.

keys.tooltip: Equipment durability loss multiplier.
Item weight multiplier.
Perishable-item decay speed multiplier.
Hours for a Huge Egg to hatch (other eggs scale from it). 0 = instant.
keys.gotcha: Default VERIFIED 1.0 hours against the 1.0.1 template (changed from EA's 72). An EA-carryover config still contains 72 and keeps using it — the classic 'my eggs still take forever' report.

keys.tooltip: Maximum players per guild.
Minutes before a player may rejoin a guild after leaving.
Days an offline guild master keeps leadership before it auto-transfers to an active member.
keys.gotcha: Fixes guilds frozen by an absent leader — one of the best 1.0 additions for community servers.

keys.tooltip: How often the server checks for an inactive guild master (seconds).
Ranch/grazing production speed multiplier.
Minutes between meteorite/supply drops.
keys.gotcha: Widely reported as ignored on dedicated servers.

keys.tooltip: Technology IDs players may never unlock (comma-separated).
keys.gotcha: Official example uses doubled quotes inside the tuple: DenyTechnologyList=(""PALBOX"",""RepairBench""). Paladin must serialize this exactly.

keys.tooltip: Cooldown in seconds before respawn after death.
If a player dies within this many seconds of spawning, the respawn-penalty multiplier applies.
Multiplier applied to the respawn cooldown when the penalty triggers.
Pals produce waste objects.
keys.gotcha: Every waste object is a live physics object on a server that already fights memory growth.

keys.tooltip: Cap on dropped items alive in the world.
Separate cap for waste items.
Hours dropped items persist before despawning.
Seconds between world autosaves.
keys.gotcha: Short interval = constant disk writes; long interval = more lost on a crash. 30 is sane.
